header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's stoa0045.stoa028.perseus-lat2, from the Perseus Digital Library (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.10.24: Every line of the original ends in a monosyllable (Ser, Sphinx, Strix, ver), which the English cannot keep. Line 10.26 is obscure: the strix is a night-bird of ill omen, and why it is “known to Caledonian wives” is unclear.

nodes.text: The Ser, flowing in robes, combs out the fleeces of the woods.
Known among three-bodied portents is the Theban Sphinx.
Known to Caledonian wives, of female sex, is the Strix,
When the year, from its rising, unlocks flower-bearing spring,
